conclusion: A bounded identity-only prepared-entry handoff is feasible in source, but no existing prepared-entry witness makes the proposed fusion safe as-is. Keep this a conditional future candidate, not an implementation or nomination.
findings: resolvedContentReferenceOrigins records only the freshly created chunk/reference object. The factory passes preparedLookupIndexes through unchanged, including foreign maps.

hasCompletePreparedTermLookupIndexes reads overridable Map.get/size and Reflect.get entry bytes/preinternedPlan. Later Map.get and entry property reads occur after the old row validation. Merely using descriptors cannot distinguish an arbitrary Proxy.

prepareTermLookupIndexesFromPreinternedPlan and native/copy parser routes already create ordinary map/entry literals. The main parser result receiver has an existing ownership-registration point before publishing its resolved chunk. Worker-local weak identity cannot survive structured clone.
The later _encodeArtifactChunkRecords validation pass is already skipped by a non-null validatedContentOffsetBase. This proposal removes only the preceding JS run-planning walk.
The twelve retained JMdict call facts belong to the exact f28 correctness receipts. This review acquired no a300 corpus or browser observation.
boundedHandoff: Use a private weak identity registry for maps/entry records created by controlled producers. At the actual worker receiver, construct/register fresh ordinary metadata wrappers before the result escapes; retain existing bytes/plan/route-filter references rather than clone payload buffers or row columns.
Do not brand an arbitrary map passed to createArtifactTermRecordChunkWithResolvedContent. A missing producer witness must return to the existing route before extra metadata reads.

Keep the existing whole-index admission/completeness calls in their original pre-row position. After those potentially effectful calls, obtain a fresh callback-free witness immediately before native selection; do not rely on a witness captured before validation callbacks.

Require the current registered map and entry, unchanged intrinsic Map has/get/size behavior, and own data fields for the metadata moved across the old row loop. Reject replacements, accessors, proxies, prototype changes, absent/null prepared bytes or plans, and a current rowCount different from the already captured count.

Reuse current per-call native input guards for actual typed brands, private non-resizable buffers, current columns and bounds. The witness establishes origin/access behavior only; it must not cache input validity across awaits.
Pass owned field bytes and computed base through the existing async encode/append boundary. Keep the existing await point and late route-filter read; do not eagerly snapshot post-await data.

A failed whole-chunk attempt must fall back to the unchanged planner and avoid a duplicate copied native attempt on the same fallback run. A call-local disposition is sufficient; no global validity cache should be introduced.
stopConditions: No controlled main-realm producer/receiver hook can distinguish owned metadata from arbitrary factory-supplied maps.
The design requires branding foreign objects by shape, deep-copying lookup/plan payloads, rechecking every row a second time, or preserving a validation witness across awaited storage work.
Run splitting, persistence formats, or session lifecycle must be redesigned.
The original browser result or later source-bound work evidence does not justify another candidate.
